“Born to Run”—Bruce Springsteen (1975)

Added to the National Registry: 2003 Essay by Cary O’Dell

Original album Original label Bruce Springsteen

“Born to Run” was Bruce Springsteen’s third album. The man who is “The Boss” has admitted that the creation of it was his blatant attempt for a true rock and roll record as well as commercial success after the tepid commercial reception of his earlier two albums, “Greetings from Asbury Park, N.J.” (1973) and “The Wild, the Innocent & the E Street Shuttle” (1973). On both counts, he got his wish. Upon its release, “Born to Run” would rise to number three on the charts. Besides gaining massive audience attention (by the end of the year Springsteen would be featured on the covers of both “Time” and “Newsweek”), “Born to Run” also saw the accomplishment of two other major factors in Springsteen’s artistic development.

Remembering Dave Marsh

Dave Marsh, longtime music historian and critic, has passed after a long illness. It was Marsh’s 1979 best-selling book, Born to Run: The Bruce Springsteen Story , which formalized Springsteen’s early career and set in motion the now library-large collection of Springsteen biographies and other works that fill the Archives’ shelves here at the Bruce Springsteen Center for American Music.
Marsh was Springsteen’s first true literary champion, recognizing in book form Bruce’s uncanny talent to unleash the power of rock & roll on the club and concert stage. Best friends with fellow critic Jon Landau at the time, Marsh and Landau both believed what Landau wrote after seeing Springsteen in a Boston club in spring 1974: “I saw rock & roll future, and its name is Bruce Springsteen.”
But Marsh’s real literary strength was music criticism. His incisive, often biting record and concert reviews pulled no punches in Creem , Rolling Stone , and the other periodicals he wrote for. He became a mentor for many a music critic who followed in his footsteps, including me.
Marsh also penned Glory Days: Bruce Springsteen in the 1980s (1987), his follow-up to Born to Run ; as well as Bruce Springsteen: Two Hearts, The Definitive Biography (2004), and Bruce Springsteen on Tour: 1968-2005 (2006). In all, he authored more than two dozen books and co-founded the influential newsletter Rock and Rap Confidential.
